report.source_text: A few days later, however, an acute confusional state prompted brain MRI. Fluid-attenuated inversion recovery (FLAIR) imaging revealed symmetrical hyperintensities strictly limited to the subcortical precentral gyrus (Fig. 1a). Correspondingly, diffusion-weighted imaging (DWI) showed signal hyperintensity (Fig. 1b), along with normal ADC and without any contrast enhancement.

report.source_text: Spinal tap revealed a normal cell count (1 leucocyte/mm3, normal range 0–4) along with slightly elevated protein (56.2 mg/dl, normal ≤50) and albumine (50.9 mg/dl, normal ≤35). CSF PCR was negative for herpes simplex virus type 1/2, varizella zoster virus, Epstein-Barr virus, cytomegalovirus, human herpes virus six, JC virus, adenovirus, enterovirus, poliovirus, and bacterial DNA (universal primer). However, repeat serum PCR for CMV showed a progressively increasing number of up to 8,600 copies/ml, starting shortly prior to the development of tetraparesis.

report.source_text: Accordingly, intravenous ganciclovir treatment (5 mg per kg per day over two weeks) was initiated. Over the following three weeks, serum PCR for CMV turned negative. Tetraparesis slowly improved, with still moderate pareses of the upper (between MRC 3 and 4), but severe pareses of the lower (between MRC 1 and 2) extremities at neurological reassessment four weeks after symptom onset.

clinician.final_diagnosis: tetraplegia was attributable to new symmetrical CNS lesions ... subacute development of tetraparesis along with new subcortical lesions in an immunocompromised patient were highly suggestive of infection by or reactivation of neurotropic viruses ... while the laboratory findings were unable to prove CMV encephalitis, they were compatible with this suspected diagnosis.
clinician.trajectory_summary: Six weeks post-stem cell transplant, patient developed high-grade pure motor flaccid tetraparesis with absent reflexes and muscle atrophy. Brain MRI revealed symmetrical hyperintense subcortical lesions in the precentral gyrus consistent with motor cortex involvement. CSF analysis was normal with slightly elevated protein but negative PCR for multiple neurotropic viruses including CMV. However, serum PCR for CMV showed a rising viral load prior to symptom onset. Patient received intravenous ganciclovir treatment with subsequent CMV serum clearance and gradual neurological improvement four weeks after onset.
